Consider the graph of the function $f(x),$ shown above. It consists of three line segments and an arc of a quarter-circle centered at $(-2,0)$ with radius $2.$ Find the value of 
${\int }_{-4}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x.$
feedback.worked_solution:
The graph consists of $4$ parts: the line segment for $x\in [-4,-2]$, the arc of a quarter-circle for $x\in [-2,0]$, the line segment for $x\in [0,1]$, and the line segment for $x\in [1,3].$ Therefore, we can write the integral as follows:

$$
{\int }_{-4}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x={{{\int }_{-4}^{-2}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{1}}+{{{\int }_{-2}^{0}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{2}}+{{{\int }_{0}^{1}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{-{A}_{3}}+{{{\int }_{1}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{-{A}_{4}}
$$

The $1$st integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-4,-2].$ The corresponding region is a square, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & ={a}^{2} \\  & ={2}^{2} \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

The $2$nd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-2,0].$ The corresponding region is a quarter-circle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & =\frac{1}{4}\pi {r}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\pi \cdot {2}^{2} \\  & =\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

The $3$rd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [0,1].$ The corresponding region is a right triangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{3} & =\frac{1}{2}bh \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 1\cdot 3 \\  & =\frac{3}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the region lies below the $x$-axis, we have 

$$
{\int }_{0}^{1}f(x)\,\text{d}x=-{A}_{3}=-\frac{3}{2}.
$$

The $4$th integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [1,3].$ The corresponding region is a trapezoid, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{4} & =\frac{1}{2}(a+b)h \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(2+3)\cdot 2 \\  & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the region lies below the $x$-axis, we have 

$$
{\int }_{1}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x=-{A}_{4}=-5.
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-4}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x & ={A}_{1}+{A}_{2}-{A}_{3}-{A}_{4} \\  & =4+\pi -\frac{3}{2}-5 \\  & =\pi -\frac{5}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
